historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 14.6% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 9.1% (EPS 5yr 13.0%). Book value is distorted by special dividends ($10/share in FY2021 depresses the start point, $15/share in FY2024 ~ $6.7bn) and by retained earnings on rising margins, so it is not a usable growth anchor; revenue 3yr (7.8%, FY2023-FY2026) is used instead, as in the prior build.
historical_growth.notes: End point is now FY2026 actual (start points FY2023 and FY2021). Owner-FCF series is reported FCF less SBC and equity-award taxes (interest income not stripped in the CAGR series because it is only split out from FY2023): FY2021 4,393, FY2023 5,668, FY2026 8,097. Owner-FCF CAGRs (3yr 12.6%, 5yr 13.0%) are slightly ABOVE reported FCF (11.6%, 11.8%), so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. FCF outgrew revenue because operating margin rose (3.4% to 3.9%) and FY2026 had an unusually large working-capital inflow; capex rose from 1.8% to 2.1% of revenue over the same period.

scenario_narratives.base: Costco keeps compounding the way it has since FY2022: ~25-30 net new warehouses a year (25 net in FY2026, up to 33 gross planned for FY2027, roughly a third outside the US over time), mid-single-digit comparable sales ex-gasoline, and digitally-enabled sales growing ~20%, so revenue grows 7-7.5% for two years and fades to 4% by FY2036. Membership fee income (FY2026 $5.9bn, +11%; renewal 92.3% US/Canada and 89.8% worldwide; executive members 42.3m) lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin from 5.04% to 5.4%, while merchandise gross margin and the tariff refunds are deliberately reinvested in price. Capex steps up to the guided ~$7.5bn (2.3% of revenue) in FY2027 while the opening cadence holds, then fades to 1.5%. This is a superb business priced as one: the base case still lands far below the market because the market capitalises Costco at roughly 50x earnings.
scenario_narratives.bull: International and digital accelerate: China, Japan, Korea, Sweden/Spain/France openings and new-country entries push unit growth toward 35-40 a year, retail media and Costco Next/ancillary services scale, and a further membership fee increase around FY2029-30 lands without denting renewal. Revenue grows 9% for two years and still 5.5% in FY2036; EBITDA margin reaches 5.9% as fee income and high-margin ancillaries outgrow merchandise. Negative working capital releases more cash as growth stays high. The market's multiple needs roughly this path plus a perpetual premium exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Growth normalises to low-to-mid single digits as US warehouse density saturates, gasoline and inflation tailwinds reverse (gasoline alone added 130bp to FY2026 sales), and e-commerce convenience (Amazon same-day grocery, Walmart+/Sam's Club at a ~$50 fee) erodes the trip frequency the membership model depends on. Tariffs and wage pressure are absorbed in price to protect the value proposition, so EBITDA margin drifts down to 4.7%; renewal rates, already off ~0.6pt from their FY2024 peak, keep slipping as younger digital-first members churn. Costco remains highly profitable and cash-generative (no solvency axis at all); the bear is a de-rating of a normal-growth retailer to a normal multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Costco is valued as an owner would: SBC and the tax cash spent net-settling equity awards are real costs, interest earned on the $21bn cash pile is excluded from the flows because the cash itself is added back, and warehouse-growth capex (stepping up to ~$7.5bn in FY2027) is charged in full. On that basis even a generous base case of ~7% growth, rising margins and a 20x exit cap values the business far below today's price, which embeds roughly 50x earnings and over 60x FY2026 owner FCF. FY2026 came in slightly ahead of the estimate it replaces, but the discount rate was corrected upward for a 10-year Treasury near 5%, so intrinsic value fell while the share price rose. The finding is unchanged: the quality is not in question, but the price assumes a perpetual premium exit multiple that the model will not grant.
key_risks_to_valuation: Exit multiple: the model caps terminal value at 20x owner FCF (22x bull); Costco has traded at 40-55x FCF for years, and if that premium persists the model understates value materially.

Discount rate: WACC moved 8.0% -> 9.0% on the risk-free rate alone; each 1pt of WACC is worth roughly a fifth of base value (see the sensitivity grid), and a fall in the 10-year yield back toward 4.3% would restore the prior figure.
Membership renewal and fee income are ~half of operating income; a decline in US/Canada renewal from ~92% would hit margins far harder than a sales miss.
Capex intensity: FY2027 guidance is ~$7.5bn (2.3% of revenue, up from 2.1%); if that level persists rather than fading to 1.5%, terminal owner FCF is lower than modelled.
Working capital: FY2026 owner FCF was lifted by improved supplier terms; the model does not assume it repeats, which is conservative if it does.
Tariff exposure on imported general merchandise (and ~$160m of IEEPA refunds still outstanding, largely to be passed to members), and e-commerce competition from Amazon and Walmart/Sam's Club.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement (COST_Annual_FY2026.txt:1474, 1493): stock-based compensation add-back 924 + tax withholdings on stock-based awards 361 (financing activities) = 1,285. Costco publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY2026 10-K weighted-average diluted shares 444.427m (52 weeks to 2026-08-30; basic 443.953m; 443.129m outstanding at 2026-09-29 per the cover page). Held FLAT because SBC (incl. equity-award taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. Costco is a steady repurchaser (FY2026 $848m cash, FY2025 $903m; $1,115m left on an authorisation expiring January 2027), so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Sunday nearest 31 August (52/53 weeks); FY2026 ended 2026-08-30
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST 5.07% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-18; it has held 4.9-5.3% since early September) + beta ~0.8 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.1% cost of equity; debt is <2% of market cap, so WACC ~9.0%. CHANGED from 8.0%: the prior build's rationale used the same beta and ERP but a ~4.3% risk-free rate, which was already ~80bp below the market at the prior valuation date. Only the observable input was refreshed; beta and ERP are unchanged. Same WACC in every scenario; risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: One treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating-lease rent sits inside SG&A, so it is already inside EBITDA and operating-lease liabilities ($2,606m at 2026-08-30) are NOT in net debt. Finance-lease liabilities ($1,413m at 2026-08-30: 94 current + 1,319 long-term) ARE in total_debt; their amortisation is in D&A and interest is below EBIT, so finance-lease principal is not deducted from the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest (Taiwan NCI bought out FY2022); none deducted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (dcf-methods routing: operating company, US consumer retailer) -- unchanged from the 2026-09-26 build. UPDATE, not a rebuild: see reconciliation. FY0 is now the FY2026 ACTUAL from the 10-K (52 weeks to 2026-08-30), replacing the prior FY2026E estimate: total revenue 303,154 (prior estimate 298,600; +10.1% YoY, of which gasoline price +130bp and FX +49bp). Year 1 is FY2027, about 12 weeks elapsed at the valuation date; Q1 FY2027 is not yet reported. Balance sheet 2026-08-30: cash 20,207 + short-term investments 1,094 = 21,301 (includes 2,842 of unsettled card receivables, which settle within four days); long-term debt 2,248 current + 3,914 non-current = 6,162, + finance leases 1,413 = 7,575; net cash 13,726. This closes the prior build's Q4 gap (its balance sheet was 2026-05-10). last_fcf is FY2026 owner FCF: OCF 15,817 - capex 6,435 = 9,382 reported, - 1,285 SBC incl. equity-award taxes - 601 interest income = 7,496 (2.47% of revenue). Interest income is stripped because net cash (13.7bn) is 1.8x the owner-FCF base; 601 is the interest-income line of 'Interest income and other, net' (711 total; remainder FX gains 69 and other 41) and includes 10 of IEEPA tariff-refund interest. FY2026 owner FCF is flattered by working capital: payables +2,755 against inventory -1,153 ('faster inventory turns and improved payment terms'), a ~10% capture on the revenue increase versus the 6% base assumption, and year 1 carries the guided capex step-up to ~$7.5bn, so the projected year-1 owner FCF (~1.8% of revenue) sits BELOW the FY2026 actual by design. Pre-SBC EBITDA FY2026: operating income 11,685 + D&A 2,674 + SBC 924 = 15,283 = 5.04% of revenue (includes 174 of IEEPA tariff refunds booked against merchandise costs, ~6bp, part reinvested in price; a further 155 received after year-end). Cash taxes paid 2,839 vs provision 3,025 (ETR 24.7%). Working capital is POSITIVE capture: Costco runs negative working capital (payables fund inventory; membership fees are collected in advance), so growth releases cash. DATA WARNING for the parser: COST_Metrics.csv / core_metrics have no FY2026 annual row and no Q4 2026 row although COST_Annual_FY2026.txt is in Extracted/ (the kpis table does carry FY2026); every FY2026 anchor here was read from the 10-K text, not the CSV. Ethics screen flagged 'tobacco' (low confidence, incidental merchandise category).

bear.capex_pct_path_note: CHANGED in years 1-2 (was 2.10, 2.00): the FY2027 programme (~$7,500m, 33 openings) is committed whatever the sales outcome, so year 1 is 2.30% and year 2 2.05% before rejoining the prior path.

base.growth_rates_note: UNCHANGED. FY2026 printed +10.1% (comparable sales ex-FX/gasoline +7%, 25 net new warehouses); FY2027 plan is up to 33 openings incl. five relocations. 7.5% for FY2027 already sits on a ~7% comp plus ~3% unit growth less the gasoline tailwind rolling off. Would move on: Q1 FY2027 comps ex-gas/FX outside 5-8%, or the opening plan slipping.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: UNCHANGED. EBITDA here is pre-SBC (operating income + D&A + SBC): FY2026 actual 15,283 / 303,154 = 5.04% (FY2025 4.97%), in line with the prior ~5.0% estimate; year 1 at 5.05%. Drifts up 35bp over ten years on membership-fee income and ancillary/advertising mix, with merchandise gross margin reinvested in price. Would move on: a fee increase, or core gross margin ex-gas moving more than ~20bp.
base.sbc_pct_path_note: UNCHANGED. FY2026 actual 0.424% (FY2025 0.455%, FY2024 0.445%); the 0.44% start is the three-year average. The withholding-tax line scales with the share price at the October vest, so one low year is not a new anchor.
base.capex_pct_path_note: CHANGED in years 1-2 (was 2.20, 2.15). FY2026 actual 6,435 = 2.12%; the FY2026 10-K guides ~$7,500m for FY2027, which is 2.30% of base-case FY2027 revenue. Year 2 held at 2.20% as the cadence of ~28 net openings continues; years 3-10 unchanged, fading to 1.5% and staying above D&A because the terminal still grows 3%.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: UNCHANGED. GAAP effective rate 24.4-25.9% FY2022-26 (24.7% in FY2026 after 155 of discrete benefits); cash taxes paid 2,839 vs 3,025 provision. No carryforward or one-off to ramp.
base.wc_capture_note: UNCHANGED at 6%. FY2026 capture was ~8-10% of the revenue increase, helped by a step-change in supplier payment terms that does not recur each year; FY2023-25 ran 7.5-12.5%, FY2022 was negative. Would move up on a second consecutive year at or above 8% without a terms change.

bull.capex_pct_path_note: UNCHANGED: 2.30% of bull-case FY2027 revenue is $7.6bn, already consistent with the ~$7.5bn guide.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED from the prior build. Bear 15%: no balance-sheet, refinancing or single-customer risk and a 40-year record of renewal rates near 90%, so the downside is slower growth, not impairment. Base 50%: the path continues the FY2022-26 cadence, which the FY2026 actuals confirmed. Bull 35%: the house default, kept because the bull needs one mechanism Costco has repeated every ~5-6 years (a fee increase) plus sustained international unit growth, both within management's demonstrated control.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
